note: What a piece is worth back (#184, D2), as one file two engines answer to. Python reads it from tests/test_sell_refund_vectors.py, TypeScript from src/till/refund.vectors.test.ts, and neither may be 'fixed' by editing this file - a case changes only when the rule changes, and then it changes for both at once. The reason is the same one the GSTIN vectors give: the counter works out a refund offline, on a bill it is about to print, and the accept pipeline then works it out again and refuses the whole bill where the two differ by a single paisa - with the customer gone and every bill behind it stopped in the queue.
rule: refund(paid, line_qty, returning, returned_qty, returned_paise) = paid - returned_paise when returned_qty + returning >= line_qty (the last of a line settles the remainder), else round-half-up(paid * returning / line_qty). Half-up in integers, never a float and never banker's rounding.

cases.why: the whole of a single-piece line - what the customer paid, to the paisa
the whole of a multi-piece line at once
one of three, where the share does not divide - 999.67 rounds half-up to 1000, and banker's rounding on a float would pay 999
the second of the same three - still a share, still rounded up
the last of the three settles the remainder, so the parts sum to exactly what was paid rather than leaving a paisa in the books for ever
an exact half - 5.5 paise a piece - goes up, which is the rounding the shop floor uses and the rounding banker's would not
two of five at once, sharing rather than settling
the rest of that line afterwards - the remainder, not three more shares
a piece already partly given back by the *other* route - the exchange leg and the plain return share one ledger, so the arithmetic cannot tell them apart and must not try
a line the books priced at nothing gives back nothing - a sold-before-inward piece the counter billed off the tag at nought would otherwise refund a garment nobody paid for
